megabase_rerun.note: Same-database, same-machine comparison after the Chess960/standard castling-rights fix (rook_file mirrors upstream setup_board; generated Chess960 starts use their own king/rook files). Full PGN export was not re-run: /tmp filled during the earlier attempt (2.6 GiB partial ours.pgn, 5.3 GiB partial upstream.pgn); SAN parity below covers exact-output on the sampled games instead.

ours_decode.verdict: all move-decode counters match upstream exactly (plies, nulls, EP, promo captures, chess960, setups); ~1.27x slower single-threaded (67.6 s vs 53.3 s), inside the pgn 1.2x-adjacent range but over the decode 'not slower' budget; 3.0 MiB peak RSS vs 13.5 MiB upstream

megabase_rerun.failure_delta: the 4 missing failures are all upstream annotation-position failures (.cba phase 4, not ported): 2455498 (size out of range), 5614728/5614732/5614734 (annotations at position 0 in games without moves). The 5 move-decode failures match upstream byte-for-byte (489834, 3079389, 3079410, 7168922, 8076798)
megabase_rerun.san_sample: 14 sampled games (ids 1-2, 2601298-2601308 incl. the Chess960 811 castling games, 2602603, last 2 records): 13/14 main lines identical to cbtool pgn; the one diff (2601298) is our sample emitting the main line only while upstream movetext continues into variations past ply 21

fast_decode_and_parallel_replay.machine: MacBookPro18,2 (Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, 32 GB RAM)

sequential_batch_decode.verdict: Single-thread throughput beats upstream cbtool verify on identical hardware (214,762 rec/s vs 209,357 rec/s); 100% counter parity

parallel_batch_decode.verdict: Multi-threaded replay reaches 1.53M rec/s (7.3 s for 11.15M games and 883M plies) - beating upstream by 7.3x
